items.questionText: A newborn baby refuses breast milk since the end day of birth but accepts glucose water. He develops vomiting and severe jaundice by the 5th day. Benedict's test was positive for urine and blood glucose was low. The most likely cause is due to the deficiency of:
items.explanationText: The clinical features on ingestion of breast milk at birth suggest classical galactosemia, a disorder of galactose metabolism. Galactose-1-phosphate uridyl transferase deficiency leads to classical galactosemia. It is autosomal recessive. Clinical features include accumulation of galactose-1-phosphate in liver causing liver damage and hepatomegaly, vomiting, and convulsions; depletion of inorganic phosphate causing diminished ATP synthesis and hypoglycemia; accumulation in nerves causing intellectual disability; and accumulation of galactitol in the lens causing an oil-drop cataract. Urinary reducing sugar (Benedict's test) and the Mucic acid test are positive. Treatment is a galactose-free diet.

items.questionText: Which of the following amino acids has an imino ring?
items.explanationText: Proline is an amino acid with an imino ring. The distinctive cyclic structure of the side chain of proline gives it exceptional conformational rigidity as compared to other amino acids. Hence, proline plays a major role in collagen stability.

items.metadataTitle: Tryptophan structure with indole group highlighted
items.questionText: A 45-year-old woman presents with loose stools, memory loss, and rashes over sun-exposed areas. On examination, a Casal's necklace lesion was identified. What group does the amino acid she is deficient in contain?
items.explanationText: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of pellagra which can be seen in the deficiency of the amino acid tryptophan. Tryptophan contains an indole group. The source shows the structure of tryptophan with the indole group marked.

items.questionText: Which special group is present in arginine?
items.explanationText: Guanidine is present in arginine. The source shows the structure of arginine indicating the guanidine group.

items.questionText: Which of the following amino acids is the most sterically flexible?
items.explanationText: Glycine is the smallest amino acid with R group as H atom. So, as it has no R group, it increases the flexibility of the protein. Proline and glycine are frequently found in beta turns.

items.metadataTitle: Nitric oxide synthesis from arginine reaction
items.explanationText: Nitric oxide is synthesized from arginine by a calcium-dependent reaction catalyzed by NO synthase. The co-enzymes of NO synthase include FMN, FAD, heme, and tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4). The source includes the arginine → citrulline + NO reaction diagram.

items.questionText: Tetrahydrobiopterin is a coenzyme for all of the following except:
items.explanationText:
Tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) is a coenzyme for the following enzymes:
• Phenylalanine hydroxylase
• Tyrosine hydroxylase
• Tryptophan hydroxylase
• Nitric oxide synthase
Tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) resembles folic acid, but it is not a vitamin. It is derived from GTP.

items.questionText: The primary structure of a protein refers to _____.
items.explanationText: The primary structure of a protein refers to the linear structure and order of the amino acids present. There are four known levels of protein structure: Primary — a linear sequence of amino acids in the polypeptide chain; Secondary — folded and geometrically ordered units of short segments of polypeptides, e.g. alpha helix, beta-pleated sheets, loops, and bends; Tertiary — secondary structures arranged into larger functional units; Quaternary — different types of polypeptides arranged in a spatial manner.

items.questionText: Which of the following is false regarding alpha helix?
items.explanationText: Alpha helix is stabilized primarily by intra-chain hydrogen bonds. Alpha helix is the most common and stable secondary structure of protein. It is a rigid, right-handed spiral. A complete turn contains an average of 3.6 aminoacyl residues and the rise per turn (pitch) is 0.54 nm. Large numbers of charged amino acids (glutamate, aspartate, histidine, lysine, and arginine) disrupt the helix by forming ionic bonds or by electrostatically repelling each other.

items.questionText: What is the most common and stable conformation for a polypeptide chain?
items.explanationText: The most common and stable conformation for a polypeptide chain is alpha helix. The alpha helix has high stability due to a large number of hydrogen bonds and van der Waals interactions between amino acids. Hemoglobin and myoglobin are proteins whose major secondary structure is the alpha helix.

items.questionText: Rossmann fold-associated NADH domain is found in _____.
items.explanationText: Rossmann fold-associated NADH domain is found in lactate dehydrogenase. Rossmann fold is an N-terminal NAD(P)+-binding domain. It is seen in lactate dehydrogenase, alcohol dehydrogenase, glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase, malate dehydrogenase, D-glycerate dehydrogenase, 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase, and formate dehydrogenase.
